title: Higher Norm from Minimum Atom Mass
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable. Suppose $X$ is supported almost everywhere on a finite set whose points each have probability at least $\lambda$, and let $q>2$ and $\lambda>0$. Then the real-valued extended-norm conversion specified by $N_r(X)=(\|X\|_{L^r(\mu)})_{\mathbb R}$ satisfies $N_q(X)\le (1/\lambda)^{1/2-1/q}N_2(X)$.
hypotheses_covered: X is a real-valued function on Ω
X has a finite almost-everywhere support whose point masses are at least λ
caveat: The conclusion uses a specific conversion of extended-valued Lp norms to real numbers; the supplied informal definition describes this conversion, but its notation is not standard.
replaced: Let $q>2$ and $\lambda>0$. Let $X$ be a measurable real random variable on a probability space, supported almost surely on a finite set whose listed atoms all have probability at least $\lambda$. Then $\|X\|_q\le(1/\lambda)^{1/2-1/q}\|X\|_2$.
